paperTitle: A Hybrid Rendering Approach for Fast and Realistic Reflections in Dynamic Scenes
centralContribution: This work presents a hybrid rendering approach for generating fast and realistic reflections in highly dynamic scenes with both rigid and deformable body simulations. It combines Screen Space Reflections (SSR) with a custom GPU ray tracing algorithm developed in CUDA, demonstrating improved efficiency and scalability compared to prior OptiX-based implementations, while achieving interactive frame rates and high visual fidelity, even with multiple reflection bounces.

gameObjects.visualMetaphor: The paper's core innovation is a hybrid rendering technique combining Screen Space Reflections (SSR) with a custom CUDA-based GPU ray tracer. This approach aims to achieve fast and realistic reflections in highly dynamic scenes involving both rigid and deformable body simulations, outperforming prior OptiX-based methods in efficiency and scalability, while maintaining interactive frame rates and high visual fidelity with multiple reflection bounces.
gameObjects.whyThisFive: This unit highlights the main achievement and innovation of the research, serving as the core message of the exhibit.

gameObjects.visualMetaphor: The paper addresses the computational challenge of achieving realistic real-time reflections in highly dynamic scenes. Traditional ray tracing is too costly, and existing hybrid methods or SSR have limitations like being restricted to static scenes, causing artifacts, or failing to integrate well with complex physics simulations, especially for deformable objects. The proposed solution integrates SSR with a custom CUDA GPU ray tracer and the Bullet Physics engine, employing a three-step process: initial SSR, followed by ray tracing for unsolved pixels (with multi-bounce support), and final image composition with Gaussian blur. A Linear Bounding Volume Hierarchy (LBVH) is used for efficient acceleration structure updates in dynamic scenes. This system aims for realistic reflections of various object types at interactive rates on accessible hardware.
